title: AI Agile Standards
description: Schema for standards/*.json files loaded by the coder and pr-reviewer agents. Each file is either a StandardsFile (array of enforceable rules) or an AdrsFile (registry of approved exceptions). See docs/product/agile/14-standards.md.

Scope.description: 'org' — lives in the ai-coding-standards2 submodule and applies to all consuming repos. 'project' — lives in the consuming repo and is additive to the org set.

Category.description: The concern domain this file governs. Must match the category prefix in every STD ID in this file (e.g. 'architecture' → STD-ARCH-*).

id.description: Unique identifier, e.g. STD-ARCH-001. Stable — never reused even if the standard is retired.

description.description: One or two sentences stating precisely what is required or forbidden.

rationale.description: One or two sentences explaining why. May cite a source file or section.

acceptance_criteria.description: Concrete, diff-checkable statements. Each starts with a subject and verb.

anti_patterns.description: Specific examples of what violates this rule.

adr_overridable.description: true — a project ADR citing this STD ID can waive a violation (finding becomes Informational). false — always blocks merge; no ADR can waive this standard.

applies_to.description: Which pipeline agents load and enforce this standard.

source.description: Optional migration provenance, e.g. 'Migrated from CLAUDE.md — §Principles'.

instantiates.description: Optional. The parent (usually org) standard ID this standard is a concrete project-specific instance of.

related.description: Optional. Other standard IDs that are related or should be consulted together with this one.

id.description: ADR-NNN — zero-padded, sequential within this file's scope.

authorises_exception_to.description: The STD IDs this ADR waives. Only standards with adr_overridable: true can be listed here.
